# List approach

**Do we use lists, and what kind?** · [all approaches](index.md) · clashes: C3, C20


## No generic lists
<a id="no-lists"></a>

Skip 'top 3' and 'three ways to'; build on takes, epiphanies and stories instead.

**Looks like:** Instead of '3 chest exercises', one opinion: 'Dips build more chest than bench for most people.' One idea, defended.

**Good at:** originality; personality; comments

**Weak at:** loses an easy, proven reach format; harder to ideate

**Best for:** formats reel30, reel60, yt-short · niches all · goals comments, trust, follows · effort low

**How:** Turn each list idea into one take, then use the Yap Map.

**Backed by:** [Avoid generic lists and motivation speeches](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-avoid-generic-lists), [Five yap frameworks; three carry 90%](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-takes-epiphanies-story), [Gym formats to rotate](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-gym-rotation-formats), [Gym angles: chest, shoulders, arms, abs](../topics/filming.md#film-angles-chest), [Outlines and mechanisms: blitz, storytime, opinions](../topics/story.md#story-controversial-outline) · sources L06

## 4–5 mini takes
<a id="list-of-takes"></a>

A list where every item is a strong take: 'Observations I made at X as a Y'.

**Looks like:** '5 things I noticed at my first LAN event.' Each item is a 6–10 s mini video with its own opinion, and the viewer stays for the next one.

**Good at:** retention; structure plus personality; comments on single items

**Weak at:** each item must be strong; longer reels

**Best for:** formats reel60, reel90, yt-short · niches all · goals retention, comments · effort medium

**How:** Number each take with an n/5 badge. A whoosh plus a punch-in at each new item.

**Backed by:** [4 or 5 mini takes](../topics/story.md#story-4-5-things), [n/3 progress badges in list videos](../topics/effects.md#fx-progress-badges), [Pick one goal: comments, sends or saves](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-conversation-goal), [Warning hook: never start X without these N things](../topics/hooks.md#l11-warning-hook), [Five yap frameworks; three carry 90%](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-takes-epiphanies-story) · sources L06

## Numbered blitz / utility listicle
<a id="blitz-listicle"></a>

Rapid-fire useful items: '9 travel hacks', '3 tools'. Tristan: even 'here's three things' beats no frame.

**Looks like:** 1/3, 2/3, 3/3 badges pop in. Each item gets 5–8 s with a visual and a pop SFX. A summary card at the end invites a screenshot.

**Good at:** reach; saves; easy to script; clear promise

**Weak at:** 'kind of cringe' (Briar); generic if the items are common knowledge

**Best for:** formats reel30, reel60, carousel, yt-short · niches all · goals reach, saves · effort medium

**How:** HyperFrames progress badges and item cards, or CapCut text templates. Keep one visual per item. Hook template (L11): 'These are the 5 best ways to use [X]'; flash the numbered menu in the first 2 s.

**Backed by:** [Even "here's three things" beats no frame](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-any-framework-beats-none), [Outlines and mechanisms: blitz, storytime, opinions](../topics/story.md#story-controversial-outline), [n/3 progress badges in list videos](../topics/effects.md#fx-progress-badges), [Promise a numbered list or a download](../topics/story.md#story-promised-list-open-loop), [Challenge, ranking and list templates](../topics/hooks.md#l11-classic-hook-templates), [Visual table of contents in the first 2 s](../topics/hooks.md#l11-toc-intro) · sources L08, L07, L02, L11

## Rating / tier list
<a id="tier-list"></a>

A list where each item gets a score or tier, ending on the full table.

**Looks like:** Six CPUs, each with a price and an x/10 verdict. The full tier table flashes at the end (sometimes held back for a comment CTA).

**Good at:** comments; saves; series potential

**Weak at:** needs authority; the table can be too small to read

**Best for:** formats reel60, reel90, carousel · niches tech, gaming, gym · goals comments, saves · effort medium

**How:** HyperFrames tier board or chart. Score reveal with a hit SFX. Open with 'Rating [X] so you don't waste your [Y]' (L11).

**Backed by:** [Verdict first: name, price, score](../topics/hooks.md#hook-verdict-first), [Withhold the rest: "comment for the rest"](../topics/growth.md#growth-withheld-remainder), [Challenge, ranking and list templates](../topics/hooks.md#l11-classic-hook-templates), [Content funnel: top, middle, bottom](../topics/growth.md#growth-content-funnel) · sources R1, L11

## List as a carousel
<a id="carousel-list"></a>

Put the list in slides instead of a reel. Caleb saw listicles do better as carousels.

**Looks like:** Slide 1 hook, slide 2 a second hook, then one image plus one or two sentences per item. Readers swipe at their own pace and save it.

**Good at:** saves; readability; a second chance via slide 2

**Weak at:** less reach than reels; needs good images

**Best for:** formats carousel · niches all · goals saves, shares · effort low

**How:** 1080×1350 slides from Canva or HyperFrames stills. One idea per slide.

**Backed by:** [Carousel: one image + 1–2 sentences](../topics/text.md#text-carousel-one-image), [Carousel: hook on slides 1 and 2](../topics/hooks.md#hook-carousel-slides-1-2), [Waterfall and repurpose winners](../topics/growth.md#growth-waterfall), [Visual table of contents in the first 2 s](../topics/hooks.md#l11-toc-intro) · sources L05, SP

## Mixing
A list of takes is the bridge between both sides (structure plus opinion). A reel blitz can be waterfalled into a carousel list.

## Rule of thumb
Reach and saves: blitz or carousel. Comments: tier list or list of takes. Personality and trust: no lists.
